lines.en: Lesson 7
lines.zh: 第7课

lines.en: Mutilated Ladies
lines.zh: 残损的钞票

lines.en: Why did Jane cook John's wallet?
lines.zh: 简为什么要烹调约翰的钱包？

lines.en: Has it ever happened to you?
lines.zh: 你有过这种经历吗？

lines.en: Have you ever put your trousers in the washing machine and then remembered there was a large bank note in your back pocket?
lines.zh: 你是否曾经把裤子放进洗衣机里，然后才想起你的后裤袋里有一张大额钞票？

lines.en: When you rescued your trousers, did you find the note was whiter than white?
lines.zh: 当你把裤子拿出来时，是否发现那张钞票比雪还白？

lines.en: People who live in Britain needn't despair when they make mistakes like this (and a lot of people do)!
lines.zh: 在英国居住的人们犯了这种错误不必绝望（而且很多人都会犯这种错误）！

lines.en: Fortunately for them, the Bank of England has a team called Mutilated Ladies
lines.zh: 对他们来说幸运的是，英格兰银行有一个名为“残钞处理小组”的团队，

lines.en: which deals with claims from people who fed their money to a machine or to their dog.
lines.zh: 处理那些把钱喂给机器或喂给狗的人提出的索赔。

lines.en: Dogs, it seems, love to chew up money!
lines.zh: 看来狗很喜欢嚼钱！

lines.en: A recent case concerns Jane Butlin whose fiance, John, runs a successful furniture business.
lines.zh: 最近有一件事是关于简·巴特林，她的未婚夫约翰经营着一家成功的家具公司。

lines.en: John had a very good day and put his wallet containing ￡3, 000 into the microwave oven for safekeeping.
lines.zh: 约翰那天生意很好，就把装有3000英镑的钱包放进了微波炉里，以求安全。

lines.en: Then he and Jane went horse-riding.
lines.zh: 然后他和简去骑马了。

lines.en: When they got home, Jane cooked their dinner in the microwave oven and without realizing it, cooked her fiance's wallet as well.
lines.zh: 他们到家后，简在微波炉里做了晚餐，并且在不知不觉中，也把她未婚夫的钱包给煮了。

lines.en: Imagine their dismay when they found a beautifully-cooked wallet and notes turned to ash!
lines.zh: 想象一下当他们发现一个“烹调精美”的钱包和变成灰烬的钞票时，他们的沮丧！

lines.en: John went to see his bank manager who sent the remains of wallet and the money
lines.zh: 约翰去见了银行经理，经理把钱包和钱的残余部分

lines.en: to the special department of the Bank of England in Newcastle: the Mutilated Ladies!
lines.zh: 送到了英格兰银行在纽卡斯尔的特别部门：残钞处理小组！

lines.en: They examined the remains and John got all his money back.
lines.zh: 他们检查了残余物，约翰拿回了他所有的钱。

lines.en: 'So long as there's something to identify, we will give people their money back,' said a spokeswoman for the Bank.
lines.zh: “只要有可识别的部分，我们就会把钱还给人们，”银行的一位女发言人说。

lines.en: 'Last year, we paid ￡1.5 million on 21,000 claims.'
lines.zh: “去年，我们为21000份索赔支付了150万英镑。”
